claims.text: Calling toString on an Output<T> in Pulumi produces placeholder text like 'Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported' instead of the resolved value, appearing in log lines, generated files, or resource properties.
A page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ titled 'Output value errors' that covers this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
The Pulumi 'Output value errors' troubleshooting page describes multiple symptoms (not only the toString placeholder message) of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
A troubleshooting page exists at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ covering errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
In Pulumi programs, stringifying an output value, branching on it (e.g., in a conditional), or reading it as if it were a plain value causes errors.

The Pulumi Cloud/CLI can return the error "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" when a stack update is already in progress, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors, and the page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/server-errors/ exists.
Post-step event failures can be caused by engine bugs; page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/post-step-errors/ exists.
Page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/connection-issues/ exists.

The Pulumi CLI produces `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` errors when it can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, documented at the #error-reading-pulumimetayaml anchor of /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/using-a-diy-backend/.
Page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/destroy-failures/ exists and covers scenarios when `pulumi destroy` fails.
Page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/interrupted-updates/ exists.
On Apple Silicon Macs, running x86_64 binaries under Rosetta 2 can cause crashes or hangs with Pulumi.
Page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/troubleshooting/ exists.
Page /docs/iac/operations/stack-management/editing-state-files/ exists and describes safe techniques for modifying Pulumi state files.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports limiting operations to specific resources with the `--target` and `--exclude` flags.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging and diagnostics, documented at /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/.
Pulumi provides pre-release dev builds that can be installed to access bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team, and the logging guide has an #automatic-logging anchor.
Pulumi has a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com that provides community support.
Pulumi offers paid support options.
The /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ page is the new update conflict page, replacing the #conflict section, per pulumi/pulumi issue 20846.
The verbose logging content moved to /docs/iac/operations/debugging/logging/#cli-verbose-logging, per pulumi/docs issue 16985.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the resource providing them has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.

The linked documentation pages exist: /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/, /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/, /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences, and /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.

When an Output is converted to a string directly (concatenated or logged) instead of via apply or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default and instead silently substitutes a placeholder message in place of the value.

In TypeScript, interpolating an Output in a template string produces a string containing literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an Output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.

In Python, formatting an Output in an f-string produces a string containing literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning without raising an exception.
In Python, passing an Output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
Python's Pulumi SDK provides `Output.json_dumps()` for serializing outputs to JSON.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error rather than a runtime surprise.
In Go, output values are resolved with `ApplyT`.

In C#, interpolating an Output in a string produces a string containing literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`, without throwing an exception.
Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` makes the string-conversion mistake throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning the placeholder text.
The `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING` environment variable is supported in TypeScript, Python, and C# (but not Go).
When Output-to-string conversion produces placeholder text, `pulumi up` still succeeds.
`pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` are string-composition helpers for Outputs in TypeScript.
`Output.concat`, `Output.format`, and `Output.json_dumps` are string-composition helpers for Outputs in Python.
`pulumi.Sprintf` and `pulumi.JSONMarshal` are string-composition helpers for Outputs in Go.
`Output.Format` is a string-composition helper for Outputs in C#.

A value read inside an `apply` callback is only available inside that callback; the callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned within it is still `undefined` when read earlier.
The apply callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix reading an outer variable assigned inside apply.
Most resource inputs accept Outputs as well as plain values, so an Output can be passed directly (e.g. `bucket: bucket.bucketName` on `aws.s3.BucketObject`) without apply.

In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on an Output evaluates the Output object rather than its eventual value and is generally always true; in a statically typed language it is usually a compile error because an `Output<bool>` is not a `bool`.
Values known when the program starts, such as stack configuration read with `pulumi.Config`, environment variables, or hardcoded flags, are plain values that can be branched on normally.
When a branch depends on a resource's Output, the branch must move inside `apply`, deriving a new Output whose value depends on the branch (e.g. `vpc.vpcId.apply(...)`).
Passing an Output as a resource's logical name, a map key, or a loop bound fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#, where these positions are typed as plain strings or numbers.
In Python, passing an Output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an Output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an Output as a dictionary key does not raise; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the Output object itself, so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.

Resources whose names or counts depend on data unknown until an earlier resource is provisioned can be restructured into a later, separate stack that consumes the first stack's outputs through a `StackReference`.

Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and synchronously pull a resolved value out of an Output; awaiting or synchronously reading an Output either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
A `StackReference` from another Pulumi program consumes one stack's outputs as another stack's inputs.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go).
